payload.name: Extract explicit advice and belief statements during ingestion
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly tells another person what they should believe, value, or remember about themselves, extract that statement as a memory candidate instead of treating it as casual encouragement.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, encouragement, or belief statements directed from one participant to another as candidate memories when they express a durable principle (e.g., worth, ability, identity). Do not skip them just because they are motivational or not a past event.
Extract the core message as a concise third-person statement attributed to the speaker, preserving the target of the advice, so future questions about what was said can be answered.

solves: The diagnosed failure was an ingestion stage that produced no candidate for an explicit statement of belief and advice, leaving a later question about that belief unanswerable. The reusable mechanism is that supportive, motivational remarks can carry durable facts or values that need memory extraction. This applies to any future conversation where one participant states what another should believe about themselves, generalizing across topics such as self-worth, confidence, or other personal attributes.
